title: Counit transposes for finite exceptional composition
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y,Z$, and smooth $k$-morphisms $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring $R$, use ordinary uncompleted constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\mathcal C_{T,R}=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ for bounded intrinsically constructible finite-Tor complexes [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], and $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}\dashv H_{h,R}=h_R^!$ with counit $\varepsilon_{h,R}$ for $h=f,g,gf$ [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation]. Compactifications are coefficient independent.

For $R=A,B$ let $\alpha_R:F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{gf,R}$ be the proper/open normalized compact-support compositor, namely the transport of the etale compositor through the canonical proper counit mates and open-extension site comparisons [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons, lem-sp-finite-compact-site-coherence]. Let $A\to B$ be any unital homomorphism of finite commutative $\ell$-primary rings, and put $S_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $b_h:S F_{h,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h,B}S$ and $c_h:S H_{h,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{h,B}S$ be the specified maps of [det-sp-reduction-direct-image, det-sp-reduction-exceptional], so that
$$\varepsilon_{h,B}(S K)\circ F_{h,B}(c_h(K))=S(\varepsilon_{h,A}(K))\circ b_h(H_{h,A}K)^{-1}.$$
Assume the compact-support coefficient identity
$$b_{gf}\circ S\alpha_A=\alpha_B S\circ F_{g,B}(b_f)\circ b_gF_{f,A}.$$

There is a unique natural isomorphism $\theta_R:H_{gf,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{f,R}H_{g,R}$ identifying the given adjunction with the composite one via $\alpha_R$. Its normalization is
$$\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_R(K)=\varepsilon_{g,R}(K)\circ F_{g,R}(\varepsilon_{f,R}(H_{g,R}K)),\qquad
\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_R(K)\circ F_{g,R}F_{f,R}(\theta_R(K))=\varepsilon_{gf,R}(K)\circ\alpha_R(H_{gf,R}K).$$
For $K\in\mathcal C_{Z,A}$ put $N=H_{f,A}H_{g,A}K$ and $D=H_{f,B}(c_g(K))\circ c_f(H_{g,A}K)$. Under the composite $B$-adjunction the transpose of $D$ is exactly
$$S_Z(\varepsilon^{\mathrm{comp}}_A(K))\circ\bigl[F_{g,B}(b_f(N))\circ b_g(F_{f,A}N)\bigr]^{-1}.$$
Consequently
$$\theta_B(S_ZK)\circ c_{gf}(K)=H_{f,B}(c_g(K))\circ c_f(H_{g,A}K)\circ S_X(\theta_A(K)).$$
These are equalities of actual $B$-linear derived morphisms for arbitrary $A\to B$, with no flatness or finite projective-dimension hypothesis.

source.place: (1)-(2), composite Hom bijections and the explicit exceptional coefficient transpose; returned proof steps 3 and 6

proof.text: Put $L_R=F_{g,R}F_{f,R}$ and $J_R=H_{f,R}H_{g,R}$. The composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] gives $L_R\dashv J_R$ with counit $E_R(K)=\varepsilon_{g,R}(K)\circ F_{g,R}(\varepsilon_{f,R}(H_{g,R}K))$. The given adjunction $F_{gf,R}\dashv H_{gf,R}$ also gives $L_R\dashv H_{gf,R}$: its Hom bijection sends $u:L_RM\to K$ to the given transpose of $u\circ\alpha_R(M)^{-1}$. Its counit is therefore $\varepsilon_{gf,R}(K)\circ\alpha_R(H_{gf,R}K)$. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to these two right adjoints of $L_R$. It supplies the unique natural isomorphism $\theta_R:H_{gf,R}\to J_R$ satisfying $E_R(K)\circ L_R(\theta_R(K))=\varepsilon_{gf,R}(K)\circ\alpha_R(H_{gf,R}K)$. This is exactly the asserted normalization, for $R=A,B$.

source.place: (1): compose the adjunctions, transport the Hom bijection along alpha, and use counit-compatible uniqueness

proof.text:
Fix $K$, and abbreviate $U=H_{g,A}K$, $N=H_{f,A}U$, $a=\varepsilon_{f,A}(U)$, and $u=c_g(K):S_YU\to H_{g,B}S_ZK$. The composite-adjunction transpose of $D=H_{f,B}(u)\circ c_f(U)$ is $T=E_B(S_ZK)\circ L_B(D)$. Naturality of $\varepsilon_{f,B}$ at $u$ says
$$\varepsilon_{f,B}(H_{g,B}S_ZK)\circ F_{f,B}H_{f,B}(u)=u\circ\varepsilon_{f,B}(S_YU).$$
Substitution followed by the assumed counit identity for $c_f(U)$ yields
$$T=\varepsilon_{g,B}(S_ZK)\circ F_{g,B}(u)\circ F_{g,B}(S_Ya)\circ F_{g,B}(b_f(N)^{-1}).$$
This uses only functoriality and the displayed hypotheses, and all four factors have their indicated sources and targets in the $B$-module categories.

source.place: (2), exceptional comparison: first expand the composite counit and use the f counit equation

proof.text:
Define the natural isomorphism $\beta_M=F_{g,B}(b_f(M))\circ b_g(F_{f,A}M):S_ZL_AM\to L_BS_XM$. Apply the assumed $g$ counit identity at $K$ to the first two factors of $T$. Naturality of $b_g$ at $a:F_{f,A}N\to U$ gives
$$b_g(U)^{-1}\circ F_{g,B}(S_Ya)=S_Z(F_{g,A}a)\circ b_g(F_{f,A}N)^{-1}.$$
Consequently
$$T=S_Z(\varepsilon_{g,A}(K))\circ S_Z(F_{g,A}a)\circ b_g(F_{f,A}N)^{-1}\circ F_{g,B}(b_f(N)^{-1})=S_Z(E_A(K))\circ\beta_N^{-1}.$$
The inverse of a composite is the reversed composite of inverses, and a functor preserves inverses. This proves the exact transpose formula in the statement.

source.place: (2), exceptional comparison: g counit equation and naturality of b_g give the explicit iterated transpose

proof.text:
Let $H=H_{gf,A}K$, $v=\theta_A(K):H\to N$, and $R_K=D\circ S_Xv$. The transpose formula just proved and naturality of $\beta$ at $v$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
E_B(S_ZK)\circ L_B(R_K)
&=S_Z(E_A(K))\circ\beta_N^{-1}\circ L_B(S_Xv)\\
&=S_Z(E_A(K)\circ L_Av)\circ\beta_H^{-1}\\
&=S_Z(\varepsilon_{gf,A}(K))\circ S_Z(\alpha_A(H))\circ\beta_H^{-1}\\
&=S_Z(\varepsilon_{gf,A}(K))\circ b_{gf}(H)^{-1}\circ\alpha_B(S_XH).
\end{aligned}$$
The third line uses the normalization of $\theta_A$ established in step 1. The last line is precisely the assumed compact-support coefficient identity $b_{gf}(H)\circ S_Z\alpha_A(H)=\alpha_B(S_XH)\circ\beta_H$, multiplied by the displayed inverses. Thus the direction of each compositor is fixed explicitly.

source.place: (2), exceptional comparison: insert theta_A and rewrite using the assumed compact-support coefficient identity

proof.text:
For $L_K=\theta_B(S_ZK)\circ c_{gf}(K)$, step 1 and naturality of $\alpha_B$ at $c_{gf}(K):S_XH\to H_{gf,B}S_ZK$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
E_B(S_ZK)\circ L_B(L_K)
&=\varepsilon_{gf,B}(S_ZK)\circ\alpha_B(H_{gf,B}S_ZK)\circ L_B(c_{gf}(K))\\
&=\varepsilon_{gf,B}(S_ZK)\circ F_{gf,B}(c_{gf}(K))\circ\alpha_B(S_XH)\\
&=S_Z(\varepsilon_{gf,A}(K))\circ b_{gf}(H)^{-1}\circ\alpha_B(S_XH).
\end{aligned}$$
The last line is the assumed counit identity for $c_{gf}$. This equals the transpose of $R_K$ computed in step 4. The composite Hom correspondence is a bijection [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], hence $L_K=R_K$, the required coefficient identity. Every operation above takes place in the given $B$-module derived categories. Only naturality, functoriality, the given isomorphisms and their counit equations were used, so no flatness or projective-dimension assumption has entered.

theorem finiteAdjointCompositorTransposes
    (ℓ p : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] [Fact p.Prime] (_hpℓ : p ≠ ℓ)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p]
    {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))] [Z.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [IsSeparated (Z ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of k))]
    (d e : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g]
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact g]
    (cf : Compactification f) (cg : Compactification g)
    (ch : Compactification (f ≫ g))
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (_hA : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ x : A, (ℓ ^ n) • x = 0)
    (_hB : ∃ n : ℕ, ∀ x : B, (ℓ ^ n) • x = 0) (φ : A →+* B)
    (DA : FiniteAdjointCompositorDatum A cf cg ch)
    (DB : FiniteAdjointCompositorDatum B cf cg ch)
    (hSX : ∀ M : spFiniteConstructibleTorCategory X A,
      spFiniteConstructibleTor X B ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ X).obj M.obj))
    (hSY : ∀ M : spFiniteConstructibleTorCategory Y A,
      spFiniteConstructibleTor Y B ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ Y).obj M.obj))
    (hSZ : ∀ M : spFiniteConstructibleTorCategory Z A,
      spFiniteConstructibleTor Z B ((scalarExtensionFunctor φ Z).obj M.obj))
    (bf : finiteAdjointSupport A cf DA.hFf ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY ≅
      reductionCtfScalar φ X hSX ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport B cf DB.hFf)
    (bg : finiteAdjointSupport A cg DA.hFg ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ ≅
      reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg)
    (bh : finiteAdjointSupport A ch DA.hFh ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ ≅
      reductionCtfScalar φ X hSX ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport B ch DB.hFh)
    (_hbf : ∀ M, (bf.hom.app M).hom =
      (reductionDirectImageComparison φ cf.i cf.g).app M.obj)
    (_hbg : ∀ M, (bg.hom.app M).hom =
      (reductionDirectImageComparison φ cg.i cg.g).app M.obj)
    (_hbh : ∀ M, (bh.hom.app M).hom =
      (reductionDirectImageComparison φ ch.i ch.g).app M.obj)
    (cfCoeff : DA.Hf ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ X hSX ≅ reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY ⋙ DB.Hf)
    (cgCoeff : DA.Hg ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY ≅ reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ ⋙ DB.Hg)
    (chCoeff : DA.Hh ⋙ reductionCtfScalar φ X hSX ≅ reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ ⋙ DB.Hh)
    (hfCounit : ∀ K,
      (finiteAdjointSupport B cf DB.hFf).map (cfCoeff.hom.app K) ≫
          DB.adjf.counit.app ((reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY).obj K) =
        bf.inv.app (DA.Hf.obj K) ≫ (reductionCtfScalar φ Y hSY).map (DA.adjf.counit.app K))
    (hgCounit : ∀ K,
      (finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg).map (cgCoeff.hom.app K) ≫
          DB.adjg.counit.app ((reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ).obj K) =
        bg.inv.app (DA.Hg.obj K) ≫ (reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ).map (DA.adjg.counit.app K))
    (hhCounit : ∀ K,
      (finiteAdjointSupport B ch DB.hFh).map (chCoeff.hom.app K) ≫
          DB.adjh.counit.app ((reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ).obj K) =
        bh.inv.app (DA.Hh.obj K) ≫ (reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ).map (DA.adjh.counit.app K))
    (hbComp : ∀ M,
      (reductionCtfScalar φ Z hSZ).map (DA.alpha.hom.app M) ≫ bh.hom.app M =
        bg.hom.app ((finiteAdjointSupport A cf DA.hFf).obj M) ≫
          (finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg).map (bf.hom.app M) ≫
          DB.alpha.hom.app ((reductionCtfScalar φ X hSX).obj M)) :
    ∃ thetaA : DA.Hh ≅ DA.Hg ⋙ DA.Hf,
      ∃ thetaB : DB.Hh ≅ DB.Hg ⋙ DB.Hf,
        (∀ K, (finiteAdjointSupport A cf DA.hFf ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport A cg DA.hFg).map
            (thetaA.hom.app K) ≫ (DA.adjf.comp DA.adjg).counit.app K =
          DA.alpha.hom.app (DA.Hh.obj K) ≫ DA.adjh.counit.app K) ∧
        (∀ K, (finiteAdjointSupport B cf DB.hFf ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg).map
            (thetaB.hom.app K) ≫ (DB.adjf.comp DB.adjg).counit.app K =
          DB.alpha.hom.app (DB.Hh.obj K) ≫ DB.adjh.counit.app K) ∧
        (∀ t : DA.Hh ≅ DA.Hg ⋙ DA.Hf,
          (∀ K, (finiteAdjointSupport A cf DA.hFf ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport A cg DA.hFg).map
              (t.hom.app K) ≫ (DA.adjf.comp DA.adjg).counit.app K =
            DA.alpha.hom.app (DA.Hh.obj K) ≫ DA.adjh.counit.app K) → t = thetaA) ∧
        (∀ t : DB.Hh ≅ DB.Hg ⋙ DB.Hf,
          (∀ K, (finiteAdjointSupport B cf DB.hFf ⋙ finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg).map
              (t.hom.app K) ≫ (DB.adjf.comp DB.adjg).counit.app K =
            DB.alpha.hom.app (DB.Hh.obj K) ≫ DB.adjh.counit.app K) → t = thetaB) ∧
        (∀ K : spFiniteConstructibleTorCategory Z A,
          (finiteAdjointSupport A cg DA.hFg).map
              (DA.adjf.counit.app (DA.Hg.obj K)) ≫ DA.adjg.counit.app K =
            (DA.adjf.comp DA.adjg).counit.app K) ∧
        (∀ K : spFiniteConstructibleTorCategory Z B,
          (finiteAdjointSupport B cg DB.hFg).map
              (DB.adjf.counit.app (DB.Hg.obj K)) ≫ DB.adjg.counit.app K =
            (DB.adjf.comp DB.adjg).counit.app K) ∧
